description: Nationwide is a leading provider of property and casualty insurance throughout the U.S. Previously known as Farm Bureau Mutual Automobile Insurance Co., Nationwide sold its first policy in 1926. In 1968, according to the company’s website, it became the first provider to offer a 24-hour claims reporting service.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
Nationwide builds its workforce with an initial focus on internships—a key pipeline for recruiting diverse entry-level employees. (In 2022, more than half of all interns were ethnically diverse, and over half were women.) Once entry-level workers join the company, the Mentorwide program offers them opportunities to network, build skills, and invest in their career development. Since the program was launched in July 2022, nearly 3,500 associates have participated, 62% of whom are women and 31% of whom are racially or ethnically diverse. 
 

Nationwide offers its associates and members of their households up to 16 free, confidential counseling sessions annually. The program has proved popular, with 27% of employees taking advantage last year compared with an industry norm of 6%. 
 

The company makes an effort to get involved with local communities, partnering with organizations such as Feeding America and the Red Cross; it contributed $3.55 million to those two organizations alone in 2022.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
The diversified insurance and financial services company makes employee education and reskilling a top priority. This marks its ninth year on the Best Companies list.

  • In the past year, Nationwide launched the MentorWide program, which connects associates to promote networking and mentorship across the entire organization.

  • The company hosts regular Catalyst for Change sessions, a safe space where employees can come together to connect and share any concerns.

  • To keep up with the changing work culture, in 2020 Nationwide made a five-year, $160 million investment in the Future of Work, a program dedicated to upskilling all Nationwide associates, who are expected to spend eight hours annually on learning new skills.

  • Nationwide launched the Future Ready Leader program in 2022 to engage the company’s leaders in a four-week educational course with opportunities to connect with peers and pursue new avenues of skill development.

  • “The culture and flexibility offered allows us the opportunity to balance life and work in a [more] meaningful way than ever before—and has helped us move into what’s now normal after the pandemic,” one Nationwide employee said.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
Founded almost a century ago, the Columbus-based insurance giant is among the most diversified insurance and financial services companies in the world. Nationwide offers a wide range of insurance plans for cars, pets, farms, and commercial purposes, as well as mutual funds and retirement plans.

  • Nationwide said 2022 was one of its strongest years ever as its revenue rose to $51 billion, up nearly 9% compared with the previous year. But its 2022 profits of nearly $1 billion marked a 39% drop from 2021.

  • Already the largest pet insurance provider in the country, Nationwide partnered with Petco Health, a pet-focused wellness company, to expand its services in the sector.

  • In April 2022, Nationwide increased its minimum wage to $21 an hour, one of the highest in the U.S.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: Nationwide employees know it’s more than just an insurance company with a catchy jingle: It’s a place where they can grow their careers. Since 2020, the company has invested $160 million in its Future of Work Center, a five-year program focused on upskilling and reskilling Nationwide’s associates. Diversity, equity, and inclusion is also a big companywide initiative, which includes programming like Cultural Fluency in the Workplace, which helps workers develop cross-cultural acumen when interacting with people from diverse cultural backgrounds and varied perspectives. “I specifically love the sense of community obligation and treating people as a whole being and not just a skill set,” says an employee. Development opportunities abound for those who work in the office, as well as for the 50% of employees who routinely work from home, and Nationwide makes an effort to keep remote workers connected to the company’s culture.

“There are so many reasons why Nationwide is a great place to work – Our caring culture, diverse workforce and love for our communities top my list. What I love the most about Nationwide is all of the volunteer opportunities we have to help our communities thrive. Not only did it feel good to do something to help others, but it was nice to connect with my team. It's opportunities like this that make me feel like I'm a part of something bigger.”

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: Founded in 1926 as a small auto insurer, Nationwide Mutual Insurance is now one of the country’s more diversified financial services companies: Its products include car, motorcycle, homeowners, pet, farm, life, and commercial insurance as well as annuities, mutual funds, retirement plans, and specialty health services. The company reported record-high total sales and premiums in 2021, as year-over-year revenue grew 13%. Nationwide also invested $350 million in financial and insurance startups in 2021. It expanded its eco-friendly portfolio over the course of the year, too, investing $173 million in renewable energy and $375 million in green bonds. The company says its own carbon footprint has decreased by almost 40% per square foot since 2010.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: As lockdowns kicked in, the share of the insurer’s workforce who worked remotely soared from 20% to 98%—in just over a week. Nationwide managed the transition with a massive dose of support, expanding paid time off for those with caregiving duties and bolstering day-care and educational resources for parents. Above all, management stayed in touch: The company says its “leader communications” rose 500%. That connection helped Nationwide rise 66 spots in our ranking. “Frequently hearing from executives gave me the reassurance to know that we were not alone,” says one associate. Nationwide aims to build on that success post-pandemic, when, it says, about 50% of employees will continue to work from home.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: The insurance giant had a challenging year. Nationwide’s net operating income decreased from $1.9 billion in 2019 to $797 million in 2020. There was also a dip in sales to $41.9 billion in 2020. Low interest rates and changing consumer behaviors were among the factors that put pressure on the company’s sales results, CFO Mark Thresher said in the company’s annual report. New technologies may be paying off, however, as Nationwide saw 30% of new auto-insurance business enrolled in its SmartRide and SmartMiles programs. By 2025, the company expects 70% of all new auto-insurance customers will sign up for policies that allow for a telematics device to be installed in their cars to record driving behavior—and encourage accident-avoidance and cost-saving habits behind the wheel.

rankings.itemDescription: After transitioning last fall to a new CEO, Kirt Walker, the insurance giant ended the year with revenues up just slightly, leading it to fall one spot in the rankings. Though there were fewer major natural disasters in 2019—which can mean costly claims for the insurer—there were numerous smaller-scale events, about 60 by the company’s count, that required it to dole out $17 billion in insurance claims and benefits. Still, Nationwide's profits surged nearly 62% last year, with a leg up from increased investment income. The company, meanwhile, continues to experiment with new technologies and to roll out innovations like SmartMiles, a pay-as-you-go auto insurance product.

rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say:


 

"Nationwide places a great focus on teamwork and having fun. We are encouraged to pursue happiness and wholeness as a measure of success. I have lunch everyday not just with my peers and direct reports, but also with my higher-ups, including executives. Our lunches are fun and it's our time to get to know one another. We refrain from work topics. This has created an atmosphere of trust and genuine care for one another. I love coming in to work everyday. My best friends are here and Nationwide is my home away from home. Plus, they have invested in my education and empowered me as a young Latina. I am able to pursue my dreams, and everyone is cheering and helping me get there."

 

"Nationwide is one of the most welcoming environments I have ever had the pleasure of being a part of. My supervisor would do anything for us: he helps us foster our growth and encourages us to do better. For example, when I don't do well on an evaluation, he never uses negative language; rather, he only asks that we try our best—it is a very freeing feeling. In addition, I can tell that upper management really cares about all of us and strives to take our opinions to heart. Since I have started working here, there have been myriad changes as a result of our Vice President listening to us—it makes me feel empowered."
